messages:
From: Emma Harrison <emma.law@harrisonllp.com>

Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus@halcyonrobotics.com>

Subject: Halcyon v3 redlines — Indemnity and evidence obligations

Kimberly / Ben —

Attached are Halcyon’s latest redlines to the Order Form and the short indemnity memo from legal (redlines_Halcyon_v3.docx). High level: Halcyon will only agree to a customer-facing indemnity for third-party IP claims where the claim arises from (i) Halcyon’s instructions to our system, or (ii) Halcyon-supplied training content. They’ve carved out open-source and downstream customer-modified prompts.

Two asks from their counsel:
- A 30-day notice window from when the customer gets notice before Redwood must accept defense or incur liability.
- A joint-evidence collection process: Halcyon wants Redwood to provide a named contact and an evidence matrix within 7 business days of a notice (we’ve attached the template).

Halcyon also flagged defense-control language (they want right-to-defend for third-party claims) and an explicit obligation to preserve logs and model inputs once notice is given. They’re flexible on limited-cost caps but want clarity on insurance offsets and subrogation.

Please confirm any absolute dealbreakers for Redwood (e.g., blanket right-to-defend or unlimited preservation obligations) and whether procurement needs the proposed SOW changes before we respond. Marcus — copying you for transparency; happy to sync after Kimberly weighs in.

Regards,
Emma Harrison
Senior Associate, Harrison LLP

Attachments: redlines_Halcyon_v3.docx, evidence_matrix_template.xlsx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Halcyon v3 redlines — Indemnity and evidence obligations

Emma / Marcus —

Thanks — I’ve reviewed the redlines and the evidence template. Quick replies:

1) Defense control: Redwood cannot broadly concede right-to-defend on third-party IP claims where the claim stems from model output; we can agree to lead defense for claims that are squarely attributable to Redwood-hosted model code or infra bugs, but customer/usage-caused claims need carveouts.

2) Notice window: 30 days to provide notice to Redwood is acceptable as a target, but we need a reciprocal confirmation that Halcyon will not amend/settle material defenses without us (or at least that we get notice before settlement).

3) Preservation: we can agree to preserve relevant request logs and the KV prefix for a limited window (e.g., 90 days) after notice, not indefinite. We will push back on obligations to preserve customer-provided datasets beyond our control.

4) Evidence matrix: we can populate the template but need Halcyon’s POC for evidence intake and a clear SLA for returns of preserved artifacts.

Ben — can procurement confirm if the proposed SOW changes (section 2.1 usage definitions + exhibit A) are acceptable operationally? If procurement wants to pause, say so — otherwise I’ll send a focused counterproposal to Harrison with our non-negotiables and two fallback positions.

Proposed next steps:
- Procurement confirm SOW (Ben / Marissa) — 24 hours
- I will draft counter with redline on right-to-defend, preservation cap, and insurance offsets — target EOD Thu (6/12)
- If Halcyon pushes back on preservation cap we escalate to CS/legal leadership for exec exception.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding Halcyon’s redlines and my notes. Action items and recommended positions below. Please treat as priority for HL-2025-007.

Key recommended positions (Redwood start point):
- Right-to-defend: Reject unilateral customer right-to-defend for model-output infringement. Accept limited right-to-defend where Redwood code or third-party model weights we onboarded are the cause; otherwise preserve right to control defense. (Rationale: operational control + insurance alignment.)
- Notice window: Accept 30-day initial notice but require Halcyon commit to not prejudge/settle without Redwood input. Add explicit cooperation covenant.
- Preservation: Offer preservations for request logs, system traces, and KV cache for 90 days post-notice. Decline obligation to preserve customer-supplied fine-tuning data or downstream derivative datasets beyond Redwood’s custody.
- Caps & offsets: Propose a per-claim cap tied to order form value (e.g., 3x annual committed spend) with usual insurance offsets and subrogation carveouts.

Procurement checklist (Ben / Marissa):
- Confirm whether SOW section 2.1 usage definitions align with our billing/monitoring — if not, return redline list with examples.
- Confirm SLA for evidence intake: Halcyon wants evidence within 7 business days; can we commit? If not, propose 10 business days.
- Approve the fallback escalation path (exec approval timeline) if Halcyon refuses preservation cap.

Sooj — CS will need to provide the operational contact for evidence intake and a short note describing what logs we can realistically produce and retention limits.

I’m drafting a succinct counterproposal to Harrison that lists: (A) our non-negotiables, (B) two compromises, (C) timeline to sign. I’ll circulate for redlines by noon.

Thanks — Kim

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Kimberly. We’re comfortable with the 90-day preservation window for Redwood-provided artifacts and the clarifying language around customer-supplied data — that addresses our biggest operational concerns.

A few quick clarifications from Halcyon side:
- We can accept Redwood leading defense for infra/model-weight defects, provided Redwood shares updated status every 14 days and does not unreasonably withhold settlement approvals.
- Halcyon will provide a named evidence intake contact (legalops@halcyonrobotics.com) and will aim to complete the evidence matrix within 7 business days; if we need more time we’ll notify promptly.
- On caps: Halcyon prefers a fixed per-claim cap tied to the order form value (we suggested 2x annual committed spend). Open to insurance offsets language.

Attached: final SOW (SOW-Halcyon.pdf) — Marcus will be the business owner. If Kimberley sends her counter, we can try to resolve one last time before routing to exec for exception if needed.

Cheers,
